Subject: MAP: Performance benchmark plan + deliverables for Finova Labs

Hi Elena —

Following our discovery session, attached is a proposed performance benchmarking plan to include in the Mutual Action Plan (MAP). The objective is to validate latency, throughput, and time-to-first-token (TTFT) under your expected concurrency profile so we can lock the SLA and close by the end of Q1. Key deliverables in the plan:

- Test matrix (model variants, sequence lengths, batch sizes)
- Load profiles (steady-state, spikes, warm/cold starts)
- Measurement targets: median latency, p95 latency, sustained throughput (tokens/s), TTFT, and observed GPU utilization
- Packaging: CSV results export, slide deck executive summary, and a live dashboard link for your ops team

Attachments: Finova_MAP_benchmark_plan_v1.pptx (slides), plus we'll deliver raw CSV and a short exec readout. Proposed timeline:

1) Week of Mar 16 — baseline runs (1–2 days), confirm test harness and sample prompts
2) Week of Mar 18 — ramped concurrency tests and edge cases
3) Mar 22 — deliver results, slides, and dashboard readout; exec sync if needed

Can you confirm Rajiv and any other infra contacts we should add for the dashboard access? Also confirm if we should include your private VPC instance for the final run or run against Redwood-hosted dedicated capacity first.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(d) +1 415-555-0122

Thanks Dylan — this looks good. A few quick asks/clarifications:

- Can you include a TTFT measurement for cold starts (first request after idle) and warm steady-state? We care a lot about first-byte latency for interactive workflows.
- Our target SLA requirement: p95 < 300ms for short chat turns (~256 tokens), and sustained throughput to support 50 concurrent agents during market open.
- Rajiv will be our infra lead; please loop him for dashboard access and credentials.
- We prefer the final acceptance run against our VPC to validate network egress and routing, but host-run is fine for early iterations.

If you can hit the dates in your timeline, we should be on track to finalize terms the week of Mar 23.

— Elena
CTO, Finova Labs

Subject: Re: MAP: Performance benchmark plan + deliverables for Finova Labs

Hi Elena / Rajiv —

We ran the plan this morning against Redwood Dedicated capacity and produced the deliverables attached: finova_perf_results_20260322.csv (raw per-request metrics) and exec_readout_finova_3-22.pdf (1-page summary + recommended config). Also published an interactive dashboard: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/finova/benchmarks/2026-03-22

Executive summary (high level):

- Test configuration: rw-3-small-8b-q4 (quantized), seq_len=256/1024, batch sizes 1/4/16 depending on profile, concurrency sweep 1–64
- TTFT (cold): median 135ms, p95 420ms (cold start variability noted; see recommendations)
- TTFT (warm): median 42ms, p95 78ms
- Latency for 256-token turns (warm): median 95ms, p95 245ms — within your p95 < 300ms target for typical short turns
- Sustained throughput: ~42k tokens/s across the pool at concurrency 32 (steady-state); single-GPU peak tokens/s shown in CSV
- Observed tail latency increases when concurrency > 48 and batch size optimization is not applied — we recommend enabling adaptive batching and a small prefix KV cache to reduce p95 by ~60–80ms for heavy burst windows

Attachments: the CSV includes per-request timing, GPU load, and exact request payloads (anonymized). The exec readout PDF highlights two recommended rollout options:

A) Host-managed Dedicated (fastest time-to-production): we can lock the SLA with a config we tested (schedule a canary and 2-week burn for audit)
B) VPC acceptance run (customer-managed): final acceptance with identical workloads to validate network behaviors — requires Rajiv to share temporary read-only access for the dashboard ingest or a scheduled run window

Dashboards include CSV export buttons and a prebuilt slide template in the shared Drive folder for your exec readout.

Let us know if you want a 30-min walk-through of the dashboard + slides today at 4pm PT — Dylan, can you confirm?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
